verdict.rationale: JumpCloud documents automated identity and access termination across the lifecycle, plus automatic offboarding workflows and HRIS-driven removal of departed employees. Nothing shows that deactivating a user kills active sessions or pushes SCIM-style deprovisioning to connected apps immediately. The instant access revocation cited in conditional access applies to network or device-compliance triggers, not offboarding, so it is not credited. Missing for 10: explicit session termination on deactivation, documented deprovisioning of accounts in connected apps, evidence the offboarding is a single immediate action, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, offboarding is one action — deactivating a user kills their sessions and deprovisions their accounts across connected apps immediately

citations.quote: Automate identity creation, access changes, and identity and access termination throughout the identity lifecycle.
establish automatic onboarding and offboarding workflows
quickly and securely onboard new employees and remove those no longer employed with minimal manual intervention and lower risk of human error
